However, maximum parallelism is obtained with EDGE_COLORING_GROUP_SIZE=1, consider using this value only if SU2 warns about low coloring efficiency during preprocessing (performance is usually worse). Setting the option to 0 disables coloring and a different strategy is used instead, that strategy is automatically used when the coloring efficiency is less than 0.875. The optimum value/strategy is case-dependent.

EDGE_COLORING_RELAX_DISC_ADJ.description: Coloring tends to perform better for the discrete adjoint than reductions because it uses less memory and enables the shared reading optimization for color loops. This option allows an automatic fallback to smaller edge color group sizes on ranks where the requested edge color group size is not efficient. Specifically, the largest edge color group size up to EDGE_COLORING_GROUP_SIZE is chosen that is at least 0.875 efficient. Also, this option allows using more colors, up to 255 instead of up to 64.

Usable with any Hybrid RANS/LES method (HYBRID_RANSLES != NONE), independent of STOCHASTIC_BACKSCATTER. With the SST_* models the production of k is corrected consistently; with the SA_* models only the momentum stresses are filtered (no k equation to correct).

FLAME_INIT.description: FLAME_FRONT initialization the flame is initialized using a plane, defined by a point and a normal. On one side, the solution is initialized using 'burnt' conditions and on the other side 'unburnt' conditions. The normal points in the direction of the 'burnt' condition. (x1,x2,x3) = point on the plane. (x4,x5,x6) = normal of the plane. (x7) = thickness of the reaction zone, this is the transition from unburnt to burnt conditions. (x8) = Thickness of the 'burnt' zone, after this length, the conditions will be 'unburnt' again.

FLAME_INIT_IGNITION.description: Flame ignition temperature in Kelvin. Specify the temperature on the 'burnt' side of the flame when using FLAME_FRONT initialization or the maximum temperature within the spark region when using SPARK initialization. The initial value of the progress variable on the 'burnt' side of the flame front is calculated through inverse regression of the ignition temperature or when reaching the upper limit of the progress variable in the flamelet data space. The SPARK_REACTION_RATES are applied within the spark region when the local temperature is below the flame ignition temperature.

FLAME_INIT_METHOD.description: Method used to ignite the solution: FLAME_FRONT : the flame is initialized using a plane, defined by a point and a normal. On one side, the solution is initialized using 'burnt' conditions and on the other side 'unburnt' conditions. The normal points in the direction of the 'burnt' condition. The 'burnt' condition is defined as the value of the progress variable for which the temperature exceeds the FLAME_INIT_IGNITION. SPARK : the solution is ignited through application of a set of source terms within a specified region for a set number of solver iterations. This artificial spark can be applied after a certain number of iterations has passed, allowing for the flow to evolve before igniting the mixture. NONE : no artificial solution ignition. SPARK is also the ignition of CANTERA_COMBUSTION= YES (Cantera detailed chemistry), see CANTERA_SPARK_TEMPERATURE. By default, this option is set to NONE

LINEAR_SOLVER_ERROR.description: Minimum error of the linear solver for implicit formulations

LINEAR_SOLVER_ILU_FILL_IN.description: Linear solver ILU preconditioner fill-in level (0 by default)

LINEAR_SOLVER_ILU_GPU_SWEEPS.description: Number of colored Gauss-Seidel sweeps used to build the GPU ILU factorization (default 2). It is not reset between calls, so with the matrix changing little between outer/pseudo-time iterations, each call refines the previous one's result instead of reconverging from scratch; for cases that do few outer iterations (e.g. elasticity problems) it may be useful to increase it up to 5.

LINEAR_SOLVER_ILU_LEVEL_SCHEDULING.description: Use level-scheduling instead of block decomposition for the ILU preconditioner. This is useful for stiff problems as it keeps the effectiveness of the preconditioner independent of the number of threads, at the expense of some parallelism (the amount of work that can be shared by the threads is reduced). This defaults to YES for elasticity problems.

LINEAR_SOLVER_INNER.description: Inner solver used for nested preconditioning (BCGSTAB is only possible with flexible linear solvers). Options: NONE, BCGSTAB, SMOOTHER Inner BCGSTAB does up to the number of iterations of the outer solver or sqrt(LINEAR_SOLVER_ERROR). Inner SMOOTHER does max(2, sqrt(LINEAR_SOLVER_ITER))

LINEAR_SOLVER_ITER.description: Max number of iterations of the linear solver for the implicit formulation

LINEAR_SOLVER_PREC.description: Preconditioner of the Krylov linear solver or type of smoother (ILU, LU_SGS, Q_LU_SGS, LINELET, JACOBI, Q_JACOBI) Q_LU_SGS and Q_JACOBI trigger the use of quantization to reduce the size of the sparse matrix (for compressible flow the matrix becomes 3x smaller relative to mixed-precision mode). Q_IDENTITY requests the same quantized matrix-vector product without any actual preconditioning (equivalent to NONE otherwise). This is only used by the compressible and incompressible solvers, others fallback silently to LU_SGS/JACOBI/NONE. A suitable nondimensionalization mode MUST be used otherwise the solver is very likely to diverge.

LINEAR_SOLVER_PREC_THREADS.description: Independent "threads per MPI rank" setting for LU-SGS and ILU preconditioners. For problems where time is spend mostly in the solution of linear systems (e.g. elasticity, very high CFL central schemes), AND, if the memory bandwidth of the machine is saturated (4 or more cores per memory channel) better performance (via a reduction in linear iterations) may be possible by using a smaller value than that defined by the system or in the call to SU2_CFD (via the -t/--threads option). The default (0) means "same number of threads as for all else".

LINEAR_SOLVER_RESTART_DEFLATION.description: Number of vectors used by FGCRODR for deflation

LINEAR_SOLVER_RESTART_FREQUENCY.description: Restart frequency for RESTARTED_FGMRES and FGCRODR

MARKER_PERIODIC.description: Periodic boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker) Format: ( periodic marker, donor marker, rotation_center_x, rotation_center_y, rotation_center_z, rotation_angle_x-axis, rotation_angle_y-axis, rotation_angle_z-axis, translation_x, translation_y, translation_z, ... )

MARKER_PLOTTING.description: Marker(s) of the surface in the surface flow solution file

MARKER_PRESSURE.description: Pressure boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker) Format: ( pressure marker )

MARKER_PYTHON_CUSTOM.description: Marker(s) of the surface where custom thermal BC's are defined.

MARKER_RIEMANN.description: Riemann boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker) Format: (marker, data kind flag, list of data)

MARKER_SHROUD.description: Shroud boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker) Format: (marker) If the ROTATING_FRAME option is activated, this option force the velocity on the boundaries specified to 0.0

MARKER_SOBOLEVBC.description: Marker for boundaries where Dirichlet boundary conditions are applied, only valid if working on the volume mesh.

MARKER_SPECIES_STRONG_BC.description: Markers where a strong BC must be applied

MARKER_SUPERSONIC_INLET.description: Supersonic inlet boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker) Format: (inlet marker, temperature, static pressure, velocity_x, velocity_y, velocity_z, ... ), i.e. primitive variables specified.

MARKER_SUPERSONIC_OUTLET.description: Supersonic outlet boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker)

MARKER_SYM.description: Symmetry boundary marker(s) (NONE = no marker) Implementation identical to MARKER_EULER.

MARKER_TURBOMACHINERY.description: Inflow and Outflow markers must be specified, for each blade (zone), following the natural groth of the machine (i.e, from the first blade to the last)

MARKER_WALL_FUNCTIONS.description: Viscous wall markers for which wall functions must be applied. (NONE = no marker) Format: ( marker name, wall function type -NO_WALL_FUNCTION, STANDARD_WALL_FUNCTION, ADAPTIVE_WALL_FUNCTION, SCALABLE_WALL_FUNCTION, EQUILIBRIUM_WALL_MODEL, NONEQUILIBRIUM_WALL_MODEL-, ... ) Reichardt's law with WALLMODEL_KAPPA and WALLMODEL_B for the wall shear stress and, on isothermal walls of the compressible solver, Kader's law for the wall heat flux, evaluated with the instantaneous solution at the exchange location: at distance h_wm along the wall normal (typically ~0.1 boundary-layer thickness, a few cells off the wall; static grids only), or at the first node off the wall if h_wm <= 0. stretching and n_points are unused.

MARKER_WALL_SPECIES.description: Wall species boundary condition marker(s) for species transport (NONE = no marker) Specify either a Neumann flux boundary condition (FLUX) or a Dirichlet value boundary condition (VALUE) for each species independently. All markers must specify the same number of species. Format: ( marker_name, BC_TYPE_1, value_1, BC_TYPE_2, value_2, ..., BC_TYPE_N, value_N, ... ) where BC_TYPE is either FLUX (Neumann) or VALUE (Dirichlet) for each species Example for 3 species: MARKER_WALL_SPECIES= (wall1, FLUX, 0.0, VALUE, 0.3, VALUE, 0.2, wall2, VALUE, 0.1, VALUE, 0.4, FLUX, 0.0) If MARKER_WALL_SPECIES is not specified, a zero-flux boundary condition will be used.

MATERIAL_REFERENCE_TEMPERATURE.description: Freestream temperature at which there is no stress from thermal expansion

MAX_BASIS_DIM.description: Maximum number of basis vectors to keep (default: 100)

MAX_DELTA_TIME.description: Maximum Delta Time in local time stepping simulations

MAX_ROE_TURKEL_PREC.description: Maximum value for beta for the Roe-Turkel preconditioner

MAX_TIME.description: Total Physical Time for dual time stepping simulations (s)

MAX_UPDATE_FLOW.description: Maximum ratio for updating density and energy variables evaluated by the linear solver relative to the non-linear solution at previous iteration. Low values ensure stability but may result in longer convergence times, based on numerical experiments Default= 0.2

MAX_UPDATE_SA.description: Same as MAX_UPDATE_FLOW but for updating nu_tilde variable in SA model, not applicable for Neg model (Default= 0.99)

MAX_UPDATE_SST.description: Same as MAX_UPDATE_FLOW but for updating TKE and Omega variables in SST model (Default= 1.0)

MESH_BOX_LENGTH.description: List of the length of the RECTANGLE or BOX grid in the x,y,z directions. (default: (1.0,1.0,1.0) ).

MESH_BOX_OFFSET.description: List of the offset from 0.0 of the RECTANGLE or BOX grid in the x,y,z directions. (default: (0.0,0.0,0.0) ).

MESH_BOX_POLY_SOL_FEM.description: Polynomial degree of the FEM solution for the RECTANGLE or BOX grid. (default: 1)

MESH_BOX_SIZE.description: List of the number of grid points in the RECTANGLE or BOX grid in the x,y,z directions. (default: (33,33,33) ).

MESH_FORMAT.description: Mesh input file format (SU2, SU2B, CGNS, RECTANGLE, BOX)

MGLEVEL.description: Max. number of multi-grid levels (0 = no multi-grid)

MG_ADJFLOW.description: Use multigrid in the adjoint problem (NO, YES)

MG_CFL_SCALING.description: Per-level CFL scaling factors for the coarse multigrid levels. Entry i is the ratio CFL(i+1)/CFL(i). If fewer values than MGLEVEL are given the last one is repeated (default 0.25, i.e. a quarter of the CFL per level)

MG_CORRECTION_SMOOTH.description: Jacobi implicit smoothing of the correction

MG_DAMP_PROLONGATION.description: Damping factor for the correction prolongation

MG_DAMP_RESTRICTION.description: Damping factor for the residual restriction

MG_IMPLICIT_LINES.description: Pave the coarse grid with advancing fronts raised from boundaries that carry a stretched layer normal to themselves (NO, YES)

MG_MIN_MESHSIZE.description: Minimum number of control volumes on the coarsest multigrid level, counted over the whole level rather than per rank, so the hierarchy does not change with the number of MPI ranks. A level holding fewer control volumes than this is not created.

MG_POST_SMOOTH.description: Max. iterations for multi-grid post-smoothing level

MG_PRE_SMOOTH.description: Max. iterations for multi-grid pre-smoothing level

MG_SMOOTH_COEFF.description: Smoothing coefficient for the Jacobi correction-prolongation smoother (default 1.25)

MG_SMOOTH_EARLY_EXIT.description: Enable early exit from multigrid smoothing when the residual RMS drops below MG_SMOOTH_RES_THRESHOLD * initial_rms (NO, YES)

MG_SMOOTH_OUTPUT.description: Print a compact per-cycle summary of smoothing iterations and residuals (NO, YES)

MG_SMOOTH_RES_THRESHOLD.description: Relative RMS reduction threshold for the multigrid smoothing early exit. Smoothing stops when current_rms < threshold * initial_rms (default 0.5)

MG_SMOOTH_STAGNATION_TOL.description: Stop smoothing when current_rms >= previous_rms * this value. Values below 1.0 exit early on stagnation, 1.0 exits only when the defect grows, 0 disables the check (default 0.99)

MG_STARTUP_CONVERGENCE.description: Full-MG promotion on convergence: orders of magnitude (log10) that CONV_FIELD must drop on the active level, relative to its value when that level became active, before promoting to the next finer level early. Negative for a drop, on the same scale as CONV_RESIDUAL_MINVAL, so -2 asks for a fall to 1% of the starting residual. Only residual convergence fields are used. Make it more negative to demand a deeper drop; a large negative value effectively disables this criterion (default -2).

MG_STARTUP_ITER.description: Number of iterations spent on each mesh during the Full Multigrid (FMG) startup phase. After this many iterations the solution is prolongated to the next finer mesh. It is also the length of the CFL ramp every level is brought up over, the finest grid included, which is what keeps the CFL from jumping when the startup hands the solution over. 0 removes the iteration budget, leaving MG_STARTUP_CONVERGENCE and MG_STARTUP_STAGNATION to decide, and disables the ramp (default 100).

MG_STARTUP_STAGNATION.description: Full-MG promotion on stagnation: if the active level's residual ratio between successive iterations exceeds this for MG_STARTUP_STAGNATION_ITER consecutive iterations, promote to the next finer level early. 0 disables (default 0.99).

MG_STARTUP_STAGNATION_ITER.description: Consecutive stalled iterations required before Full-MG promotes on stagnation. 0 disables the criterion, as MG_STARTUP_STAGNATION= 0 does (default 5).

MIN_ROE_TURKEL_PREC.description: Minimum value for beta for the Roe-Turkel preconditioner

MIXEDOUT_COEFF.description: Parameters of the Newton method for the MIXEDOUT average algorithm (under relaxation factor, tollerance, max number of iterations)

MIXINGPLANE_INTERFACE_KIND.description: Specify kind of interpolation for the mixing-plane (LINEAR_INTERPOLATION, NEAREST_SPAN, MATCHING)

MIXING_VISCOSITY_MODEL.description: mixing model for species transport (DAVIDSON, WILKE)

MOLECULAR_WEIGHT.section: NONEQUILIBRIUM GAS, IDEAL GAS, POLYTROPIC, VAN DER WAALS AND PENG ROBINSON CONSTANTS, CoolProp library
MOLECULAR_WEIGHT.description: Molecular Weights of species for an incompressible ideal gas (28.96 g/mol (air) default), For multispecies, we have N Molecular weights: W_1, W_2,...., W_N

MOVE_MOTION_ORIGIN.description: Move Motion Origin for marker moving (1 or 0)

MSW_ALPHA.description: MSW coefficient for blending states based on pressure jump. Using 0 makes the scheme average left and right regardless of pressure.

MULTIPOINT_MACH_NUMBER.description: Definition of multipoint design problems, this option should be combined with the the prefix MULTIPOINT in the objective function or constraint (e.g. MULTIPOINT_DRAG, MULTIPOINT_LIFT, etc.)

MULTIPOINT_MESH_FILENAME.description: Multipoint mesh filenames, if using different meshes for each point

MULTIPOINT_OUTLET_VALUE.description: Multipoint design for outlet quantities (varying back pressure or mass flow operating points)

MULTIZONE_ADAPT_FILENAME.description: For multizone problems, extend solution and restart filenames automatically by zone number

MULTIZONE_MESH.description: Determine if the mesh file supports multizone. \n DEFAULT: true (temporarily)

MULTIZONE_RESIDUAL.description: Determine if we need to allocate memory to store the multizone residual. \n DEFAULT: true (temporarily)

MULTIZONE_SOLVER.description: Physical governing equations Options: see Solver_Map

MUSCL_ADJTURB.description: Check if the MUSCL scheme should be used

MUSCL_FLOW.description: Monotonic Upwind Scheme for Conservation Laws (TVD) in the flow equations. Required for 2nd order upwind schemes (NO, YES)

MUSCL_KAPPA_FLOW.description: Coefficient for blending upwind and central differences in MUSCL scheme. Values range from -1 (fully one-sided) to 1 (central difference).

MUSCL_KAPPA_SPECIES.description: Same as MUSCL_KAPPA_FLOW but for species transport.

MUSCL_KAPPA_TURB.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION

MUSCL_TURB.description: Check if the MUSCL scheme should be used

MU_CONSTANT.description: Molecular Viscosity that would be constant (1.716E-5 by default)

MU_POLYCOEFFS.description: Temperature polynomial coefficients (up to quartic) for viscosity. Format -> Mu(T) : b0 + b1*T + b2*T^2 + b3*T^3 + b4*T^4

NEWTON_KRYLOV_IPARAM.description: Integer parameters {startup iters, precond iters, initial tolerance relaxation}.

NUM_METHOD_GRAD.description: Numerical method for spatial gradients (GREEN_GAUSS, WEIGHTED_LEAST_SQUARES)

NUM_METHOD_GRAD_RECON.section: COMMON PARAMETERS DEFINING THE NUMERICAL METHOD
NUM_METHOD_GRAD_RECON.description: Numerical method for spatial gradients to be used for MUSCL reconstruction Options are (GREEN_GAUSS, WEIGHTED_LEAST_SQUARES, LEAST_SQUARES). Default value is NONE and the method specified in NUM_METHOD_GRAD is used.

NUM_SPANWISE_SECTIONS.description: Integer number of spanwise sections to compute 3D turbo BC and Performance for turbomachinery

NZONES.description: Number of zones of the problem

OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION.section: COMMON PARAMETERS DEFINING THE NUMERICAL METHOD
OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION.description: Objective function in gradient evaluation (DRAG, LIFT, SIDEFORCE, MOMENT_X, MOMENT_Y, MOMENT_Z, EFFICIENCY, BUFFET, EQUIVALENT_AREA, NEARFIELD_PRESSURE, FORCE_X, FORCE_Y, FORCE_Z, THRUST, TORQUE, TOTAL_HEATFLUX, CUSTOM_OBJFUNC MAXIMUM_HEATFLUX, INVERSE_DESIGN_PRESSURE, INVERSE_DESIGN_HEATFLUX, SURFACE_TOTAL_PRESSURE, SURFACE_MASSFLOW, SURFACE_STATIC_PRESSURE, SURFACE_MACH) For a weighted sum of objectives: separate by commas, add OBJECTIVE_WEIGHT and MARKER_MONITORING in matching order.

OBJECTIVE_WEIGHT.section: COMMON PARAMETERS DEFINING THE NUMERICAL METHOD
OBJECTIVE_WEIGHT.description: List of weighting values when using more than one OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION. Separate by commas and match with MARKER_MONITORING.

OMEGA_HB.description: Omega_HB = 2*PI*frequency - frequencies for Harmonic Balance method

OPT_BOUND_LOWER.description: Lower bound for each design variable (bound in the python optimizer)

OPT_BOUND_UPPER.description: Upper bound for each design variable (bound in the python optimizer)

OPT_COMBINE_OBJECTIVE.description: Use combined objective within gradient evaluation: may reduce cost to compute gradients when using the adjoint formulation.

OPT_CONSTRAINT.description: Optimization constraint functions with pushing factors (affects its value, not the gradient in the python scripts), separated by semicolons ex= (Objective = Value ) * Scale, use '>','<','='

OPT_GRADIENT_FACTOR.description: Factor to reduce the norm of the gradient (affects the objective function and gradient in the python scripts) In general, a norm of the gradient ~1E-6 is desired.

OPT_LINE_SEARCH_BOUND.description: Optimization bound (bounds the line search in SU2_DEF)

OPT_OBJECTIVE.description: Optimization objective function with scaling factor, separated by semicolons. To include quadratic penalty function: use OPT_CONSTRAINT option syntax within the OPT_OBJECTIVE list. ex= Objective * Scale

OPT_RELAX_FACTOR.description: Factor to relax or accelerate the optimizer convergence (affects the line search in SU2_DEF) In general, surface deformations of 0.01'' or 0.0001m are desirable

OUTER_ITER.description: Maximum number of outer iterations (only for multizone problems)

OUTLIER_MITIGATION_PARAM.section: COMMON PARAMETERS DEFINING THE NUMERICAL METHOD
OUTLIER_MITIGATION_PARAM.description: For the compressible solver only (EULER, NS, RANS). Detect non-physical solutions statistically instead of relying just on zero or negative pressure or temperature, treat all points where temperature is further than N standard deviations from the mean as non-physical (MUSCL off and potentially higher dissipation). Strategy starts at inner iteration I, mean and sigma update every F, and distribution is printed every P updates.
OUTLIER_MITIGATION_PARAM.example: (I, F, P, N). With the default start iteration this is essentially off.

OUTPUT_FILES.description: Files to output Possible formats : (TECPLOT_ASCII, TECPLOT, SURFACE_TECPLOT_ASCII, SURFACE_TECPLOT, CSV, SURFACE_CSV, PARAVIEW_ASCII, PARAVIEW_LEGACY, SURFACE_PARAVIEW_ASCII, SURFACE_PARAVIEW_LEGACY, PARAVIEW, SURFACE_PARAVIEW, RESTART_ASCII, RESTART, CGNS, SURFACE_CGNS, STL_ASCII, STL_BINARY) default : (RESTART, PARAVIEW, SURFACE_PARAVIEW)

OUTPUT_PRECISION.description: Number of digits of the text outputs (SU2_DOT, history and screen). Useful for exact gradient validation. It does not change the volume and surface files (see VOLUME_OUTPUT_PRECISION).

OUTPUT_WRT_FREQ.description: list of writing frequencies corresponding to the list in OUTPUT_FILES

P1_INITIALIZATION.description: Kind of initialization of the P1 model (ZERO, TEMPERATURE_INIT)

PARMETIS_EDGE_WEIGHT.description: The work-estimate metric is a weighted function of the work-per-edge (e.g. spatial discretization, linear system solution) and of the work-per-point (e.g. source terms, temporal discretization) the former usually accounts for >90% of the total. These weights are INTEGERS (for compatibility with ParMETIS) thus not [0, 1]. To balance memory usage (instead of computation) the point weight needs to be increased (especially for explicit time integration methods).

PARMETIS_POINT_WEIGHT.description: ParMETIS load balancing weight for points

PARMETIS_TOLERANCE.description: Load balancing tolerance, lower values will make ParMETIS work harder to evenly distribute the work-estimate metric across all MPI ranks, at the expense of more edge cuts (i.e. increased communication cost).

PASTIX_FACTORIZATION_FREQUENCY.description: Number of calls to 'Build' that trigger re-factorization (0 means only once)

PASTIX_FILL_LEVEL.description: Level of fill for PaStiX incomplete LU factorization

PASTIX_VERBOSITY_LEVEL.description: 0 - Quiet, 1 - During factorization and cleanup, 2 - Even more detail

PERFORMANCE_AVERAGE_PROCESS_KIND.description: Specify Kind of average process for computing turbomachinery performance parameters (ALGEBRAIC, AREA, MASSSFLUX, MIXEDOUT) default AREA

PISO_CORRECTIONS.description: Number of pressure corrections in the SIMPLE algorithm. >1 leads to the PISO algorithm. (default = 1 = SIMPLE)

PITCHING_AMPL.description: Pitching amplitude (degrees) about the motion origin

PITCHING_OMEGA.description: Pitching angular freq. (rad/s) about the motion origin

PITCHING_PHASE.description: Pitching phase offset (degrees) about the motion origin

PITCH_NATURAL_FREQUENCY.description: Natural frequency of the spring in the pitching direction (rad/s)

PLUNGE_NATURAL_FREQUENCY.description: Natural frequency of the spring in the plunging direction (rad/s)

PLUNGING_AMPL.description: Plunging amplitude (m or ft) in x, y, & z directions

PLUNGING_OMEGA.description: Plunging angular freq. (rad/s) in x, y, & z directions

POISSON_LINEAR_SOLVER.description: Linear solver for poisson equation (same options as LINEAR_SOLVER)

POISSON_LINEAR_SOLVER_ERROR.description: Minimum error of the linear solver for poisson eq.

POISSON_LINEAR_SOLVER_ITER.description: Max. Number of iterations for the poisson linear solver

POISSON_LINEAR_SOLVER_PREC.description: Preconditioner of the poisson linear solver (same options as LINEAR_SOLVER_PREC)

PRANDTL_LAM.description: Laminar Prandtl number (0.72 (air), only for CONSTANT_PRANDTL)

PREFERENTIAL_DIFFUSION.description: Enable preferential diffusion for progress variable, total enthalpy, mixture fraction FGM problems. If 'YES', the preferential diffusion model from Efimov et al.(2021) is used for computing the viscous residual terms. If enabled, make sure the variables "Beta_ProgVar", "Beta_Enth_Thermal", "Beta_Enth", and "Beta_MixFrac", corresponding to the preferential diffusion terms of the progress variable, temperature, total enthalpy, and mixture fraction respectively are included in the manifold. By default, this option is disabled.

PRESTRETCH.description: Consider a prestretch in the structural domain

PRESTRETCH_FILENAME.description: Filename to input for prestretching membranes

PRINT_INLET_INTERPOLATED_DATA.description: Write interpolated inlet vertex data to the file Interpolated_Data_<MARKERNAME>.dat

PSEUDO_STATIC.description: Pseudo static analysis (no density in dynamic analysis)

QUADRATURE_FACTOR_CURVED_FEM.description: Constant factor applied for quadrature with curved elements (3.0 by default)

QUADRATURE_FACTOR_STRAIGHT_FEM.description: Constant factor applied for quadrature with straight elements (2.0 by default)

QUADRATURE_FACTOR_TIME_ADER_DG.description: Factor applied during quadrature in time for ADER-DG. (2.0 by default)

QUASI_NEWTON_NUM_SAMPLES.description: Enable (if != 0) quasi-Newton acceleration/stabilization of discrete adjoints

RADIAL_BASIS_FUNCTION_POLYNOMIAL_TERM.description: Use polynomial term in radial basis function interpolation.

RADIAL_BASIS_FUNCTION_PRUNE_TOLERANCE.description: Tolerance to prune small coefficients from the RBF interpolation matrix.

RADIUS_GYRATION_SQUARED.description: The radius of gyration squared (expressed in semichords) of the typical section about the elastic axis

RAMP_AND_RELEASE_LOAD.description: release the load after applying the ramp

RAMP_FSI_ITER.description: Number of FSI iterations during which a ramp is applied

RAMP_LOADING.description: Apply the load as a ramp

RAMP_MOTION_FRAME.description: Specify ramp option for frame of motion (YES, NO) default NO

RAMP_MOTION_FRAME_COEFF.description: Parameters of the frame of motion ramp (starting frame of motion speed, updating-iteration-frequency, total number of iteration for the ramp)

RAMP_MUSCL.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
RAMP_MUSCL.description: Option to ramp the MUSCL reconstruction scheme gradually from first to second order

RAMP_MUSCL_COEFF.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
RAMP_MUSCL_COEFF.description: Coefficients for the MUSCL ramp, 1st is ramp start iteration, 2nd is the ramp update frequency, 3rd is the total number of iterations of the ramp

RAMP_MUSCL_POWER.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
RAMP_MUSCL_POWER.description: Value for modifying how aggresively the ramp is applied (cannot be less than or equal to 0) < 1 = Aggresive ramp up early, slower later, > 1 slow initial ramping, more aggresive towards end

RAMP_OUTLET.description: Specify ramp option for Outlet Giles value (YES, NO) default NO

RAMP_OUTLET_COEFF.description: Parameters of the outlet Giles ramp (starting outlet value, updating-iteration-frequency, total number of iteration for the ramp)

RAMP_TIME.description: Time while the load is to be increased linearly

RBF_DATA_REDUCTION.description: Use of data reduction methods for RBF interpolated mesh deformation

RBF_GREEDY_TOLERANCE.description: Tolerance for the data reduction methods used in RBF mesh deformation

REFERENCE_GEOMETRY_SURFACE.description: If true consider only the surfaces where loads are applied.

REF_LENGTH.description: Reference length for moment non-dimensional coefficients (m or in)

REF_ORIGIN_MOMENT_X.description: Reference origin for moment computation (m or in)

REF_ORIGIN_MOMENT_Y.description: Y Reference origin for moment computation

REF_ORIGIN_MOMENT_Z.description: Z Reference origin for moment computation

REF_SHARP_EDGES.description: Reference coefficient for detecting sharp edges (3.0 by default).

RELATIVE_FRAME_SLIDINGPLANE.description: Activate sliding plane for relative frame

RELAXATION_FACTOR_ADJOINT.description: Relaxation coefficient (also for discrete adjoint problems)

RELAXATION_FACTOR_PRESSURE.description: The relaxation factor for the pressure correction (default = 1.0)

RK_ALPHA_COEFF.section: COMMON PARAMETERS DEFINING THE NUMERICAL METHOD

ROE_LOW_DISSIPATION.description: Roe Low Dissipation function for Hybrid RANS/LES simulations (FD, NTS, NTS_DUCROS)

ROM_SAVE_FREQ.description: Frequency of snapshots saves, for unsteady problems (default: 1. 2 means every other)

ROTATION_RATE.description: Angular velocity vector (rad/s) about the motion origin

SA_DES_NO_DAMPING.description: Blend the SA damping functions towards fv1 = 1, fv2 = 0, fw = 1 with the LES sensor, e.g. fv1 = (1 - f_d)*fv1 + f_d (SA-based Hybrid RANS/LES only, NO, YES)

SA_OPTIONS.section: DIRECT, ADJOINT, AND LINEARIZED PROBLEM DEFINITION
SA_OPTIONS.description: Specify versions/corrections of the SA model (NEGATIVE, EDWARDS, WITHFT2, QCR2000, COMPRESSIBILITY, ROTATION, BCM, EXPERIMENTAL)

SBS_BESSEL_SCALING.description: Scale the spatially-correlated random field using the Bessel integral, to preserve unit variance locally instead of only in a domain-averaged sense (NO, YES)

SBS_BOX_BOUNDS.description: Bounds of the box where the Stochastic Backscatter Model is activated (x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max, z_min, z_max)

SBS_DAMP_SOURCE.description: Scale the stochastic source terms (momentum and turbulence equations) by the fraction of turbulent kinetic energy that is modeled rather than resolved (SST-based Stochastic Backscatter Model only, NO, YES). If NO (default), the modeled fraction is 1, i.e. no damping.

SBS_IN_BOX.description: Apply Stochastic Backscatter Model only in a bounded box (NO, YES)

SBS_KAPPA_4TH.description: 4th order artificial dissipation coefficient of the centered flux of the Langevin equations, SBS_SOURCE_TYPE= LANGEVIN only (0.0 = no dissipation)

SBS_MAX_ITER_SMOOTH.description: Maximum number of smoothing iterations for SBS model (100)

SBS_RANS_CONSTRAINT.description: Read the turbulent kinetic energy from an external reference RANS restart file (solution_flow_RANS.dat/.csv, same mesh, same format as a normal restart), stored as a measure of the total kinetic energy. Only available for SST-based Hybrid RANS/LES models (NO, YES).

SBS_RESTART.description: Restart the stochastic field from the solution file, if present (NO, YES)

SBS_SOURCE_DIAGNOSTICS.description: Write diagnostics of the stochastic source term in the Langevin equations (NO, YES)

SBS_SOURCE_TURB.description: Include stochastic source term in the turbulence model equation (NO, YES)

SBS_SOURCE_TYPE.description: Kind of stochastic source term included in the balance equations (WHITE_NOISE, ORNSTEIN_UHLENBECK, LANGEVIN)

SBS_TIMESCALE_CONV_MAX.description: Upper bound of the LES time scale of the Langevin equations, in units of the local convective time Delta/|u| (SA-based models only, 0.0 = no bound)

SBS_TKE_STRAIN.description: Estimate the subgrid kinetic energy of the stochastic forcing as nu_t times the magnitude of the time-averaged strain rate, instead of (nu_t/(C_DES*Delta))^2 (NO, YES). The LES time scale of the Langevin equations, SBS_TIMESCALE_COEFF*Delta/sqrt(k), follows the same estimate, capped by the standard SBS_TIMESCALE_COEFF*Delta^2/nu_t where the mean strain is weak. SA-based models only, the mean quantities restart from zero unless RESTART_AVERAGE= YES. With SBS_USE_MEAN_TURB= YES the mean nu_t is used, so the source in the nu_tilde equation does not scale with nu_tilde (recommended).

SBS_USE_MEAN_TURB.description: Use a mean (time-averaged, instead of the instantaneous) turbulence quantity in the definition of the stochastic source term: the mean turbulent kinetic energy for the SST model, the mean eddy viscosity for the SA model (NO, YES). The time-averaged fields needed by the solver are added to the volume output automatically if the TIME_AVERAGE group is not requested.

SCHMIDT_NUMBER_LAMINAR.description: Laminar Schmidt number for mass diffusion (for constant schmidt number model)

SCHMIDT_NUMBER_TURBULENT.description: Turbulent Schmidt number of mass diffusion

SCREEN_OUTPUT.description: Screen output fields (use 'SU2_CFD -d <config_file>' to view list of available fields)

SEMI_SPAN.description: Aircraft semi-span (0 implies automatic calculation) (m or in)

SENS_REMOVE_SHARP.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
SENS_REMOVE_SHARP.description: Remove sharp edges from the sensitivity evaluation (NO, YES)

SENS_SMOOTHING.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION

SEPARATE_DIMENSIONS.description: Switch for running the smoothing procedure seperately in each space dimension (NO, YES).

SIDESLIP_ANGLE.description: Side-slip angle (degrees, only for compressible flows)

SINE_LOAD.description: option to apply the load as a sine

SINE_LOAD_COEFF.description: the 1st coeff is the amplitude, the 2nd is the frequency, the 3rd is the phase in radians

SLOPE_LIMITER_ADJFLOW.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
SLOPE_LIMITER_ADJFLOW.description: Slope limiter for the adjoint solution. OPTIONS: See Limiter_Map

SLOPE_LIMITER_ADJTURB.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION

SLOPE_LIMITER_FLOW.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
SLOPE_LIMITER_FLOW.description: Slope limiter (NONE, VENKATAKRISHNAN, VENKATAKRISHNAN_WANG, BARTH_JESPERSEN, VAN_ALBADA_EDGE, NISHIKAWA_R3, NISHIKAWA_R4, NISHIKAWA_R5)

SLOPE_LIMITER_HEAT.description: Slope limiter for the heat equation (same options as SLOPE_LIMITER_SPECIES)

SLOPE_LIMITER_SPECIES.description: Slope limiter for species equations (same as SLOPE_LIMITER_TURB)

SLOPE_LIMITER_TURB.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION

SMOOTHING_EPSILON1.description: Scaling factor for the identity part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator

SMOOTHING_EPSILON2.description: Scaling factor for the Laplace part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator

SMOOTH_GRADIENT.description: Activate the gradient smoothing solver for the discrete adjoint driver (NO, YES) see TestCases/grad_smooth/naca0012/inv_NACA0012_gradsmooth.cfg for a detailed explanantion on the config options shown here.

SMOOTH_ON_SURFACE.description: Switch for applying the Sobolev smoothing to the design surface mesh, i.e., instead of the whole volume mesh (NO, YES).

SOBOLEV_MODE.description: Mode how the Sobolev method is applied to the discrete adjoint gradient.

SOLVER.section: DIRECT, ADJOINT, AND LINEARIZED PROBLEM DEFINITION
SOLVER.description: Solver type (EULER, NAVIER_STOKES, RANS, LES, INC_EULER, INC_NAVIER_STOKES, INC_RANS, INC_LES, NEMO_EULER, NEMO_NAVIER_STOKES, FEM_EULER, FEM_NAVIER_STOKES, FEM_RANS, FEM_LES, HEAT_EQUATION_FVM, ELASTICITY)

SPANWISE_KIND.description: type of algorithm to identify the span-wise sections at the turbo boundaries. 1 means automatic.

SPARK_INIT.description: SPARK initialization the solution is ignited through application of a set of source terms within a specified region for a set number of solver iterations. This artificial spark can be applied after a certain number of iterations has passed, allowing for the flow to evolve before igniting the mixture. (x1,x2,x3) = spark center location. (x4) = spark radius where within the artificial spark is applied. (x5,x6) = spark iteration start and number of iterations in which the artifical spark is applied. For single-zone problems the number of iterations are inner-loop iterations, for multi-zone problems, outer-loop iterations are considered.

SPARK_REACTION_RATES.description: Source terms (density times species time rate of change) applied to the species equations in the spark region for the duration of the spark. The number of terms should equate the total number of species in the flamelet problem.

SPATIAL_FOURIER.description: YES Non reflectivity activated, NO the Giles BC behaves as a normal 1D characteristic-based BC

SPECIAL_OUTPUT.description: Determines if the special output is written out

SPECIES_CLIPPING.description: Activate clipping for scalar transport equations

SPECIFIC_HEAT_CP.section: NONEQUILIBRIUM GAS, IDEAL GAS, POLYTROPIC, VAN DER WAALS AND PENG ROBINSON CONSTANTS, CoolProp library
SPECIFIC_HEAT_CP.description: Specific heat at constant pressure, Cp (1004.703 J/kg*K (air)). Incompressible fluids with energy eqn. (CONSTANT_DENSITY, INC_IDEAL_GAS) and the heat equation.

SPECIFIED_INLET_PROFILE.description: Read inlet profile from a file (YES, NO) default: NO

SST_OPTIONS.section: DIRECT, ADJOINT, AND LINEARIZED PROBLEM DEFINITION
SST_OPTIONS.description: Specify versions/corrections of the SST model (V2003m, V1994m, VORTICITY, KATO_LAUNDER, UQ, SUSTAINING, COMPRESSIBILITY-WILCOX, COMPRESSIBILITY-SARKAR, DIMENSIONLESS_LIMIT)

STOCHASTIC_BACKSCATTER.description: Stochastic Backscatter Model (NO, YES). Requires an unsteady simulation (TIME_DOMAIN= YES), a 3D mesh and HYBRID_RANSLES= SA_DES, SA_DDES, SST_DES or SST_DDES. Not available for adjoint problems. Only translational periodicity is supported. With SOLVER= LES / INC_LES (explicit SGS model, SBS_SOURCE_TYPE= WHITE_NOISE) Leith's model (1990) is used.

STREAMWISE_PERIODIC_MASSFLOW.description: Target massflow [kg/s]. Necessary pressure drop is determined iteratively. Initial value is given via STREAMWISE_PERIODIC_PRESSURE_DROP. Default value 1.0. Use INC_OUTLET_DAMPING as a relaxation factor. Default value 0.1 is a good start.

STREAMWISE_PERIODIC_OUTLET_HEAT.description: Prescribe integrated heat [W] extracted at the periodic "outlet". Only active if STREAMWISE_PERIODIC_TEMPERATURE= NO. If set to zero, the heat is integrated automatically over all present MARKER_HEATFLUX. Upon convergence, the area averaged inlet temperature will be INC_TEMPERATURE_INIT. Defaults to 0.0.

STREAMWISE_PERIODIC_PRESSURE_DROP.description: Delta P [Pa] value that drives the flow as a source term in the momentum equations. Defaults to 1.0.

STREAMWISE_PERIODIC_TEMPERATURE.description: Use streamwise periodic temperature (default=NO, YES) If NO, the heatflux is taken out at the outlet. This option is only necessary if INC_ENERGY_EQUATION=YES

STRESS_PENALTY_PARAM.description: Parameters for the corresponding OF (allowed stress and KS multiplier).

SUBSONIC_ENGINE.description: Initialization with a subsonic flow around the engine.

SUBSONIC_ENGINE_CYL.description: Axis of the cylinder that defines the subsonic region (A_X, A_Y, A_Z, B_X, B_Y, B_Z, Radius)

SUBSONIC_ENGINE_VALUES.description: Flow variables that define the subsonic region (Mach, Alpha, Beta, Pressure, Temperature)

SUPERCATALYTIC_WALL.description: specify if catalytic wall is a supercatalytic wall

SUPERCATALYTIC_WALL_COMPOSITION.description: species composition at the supercatalytic wall

SURFACE_ADJ_FILENAME.description: Output file surface adjoint coefficient (w/o extension)

SURFACE_FILENAME.description: Output file surface flow coefficient (w/o extension)

SURFACE_MOVEMENT.description: Type of dynamic surface movement (NONE, DEFORMING, MOVING_WALL, AEROELASTIC, AEROELASTIC_RIGID_MOTION EXTERNAL, EXTERNAL_ROTATION)

SURFACE_PITCHING_AMPL.description: Pitching amplitude (degrees) about the motion origin

SURFACE_PITCHING_OMEGA.description: Pitching angular freq. (rad/s) about the motion origin

SURFACE_PITCHING_PHASE.description: Pitching phase offset (degrees) about the motion origin

SURFACE_PLUNGING_AMPL.description: Plunging amplitude (m or ft) in x, y, & z directions

SURFACE_PLUNGING_OMEGA.description: Plunging angular freq. (rad/s) in x, y, & z directions

SURFACE_ROTATION_RATE.description: Angular velocity vector (rad/s) about the motion origin

SURFACE_SENS_FILENAME.description: Output file surface sensitivity (discrete adjoint) (w/o extension)

SURFACE_TRANSLATION_RATE.description: Translational velocity (m/s or ft/s) in the x, y, & z directions

SUTHERLAND_CONSTANT.description: Sutherland constant (110.4 default value for AIR SI)

SYSTEM_MEASUREMENTS.section: DIRECT, ADJOINT, AND LINEARIZED PROBLEM DEFINITION
SYSTEM_MEASUREMENTS.description: System of measurements (SI, US) International system of units (SI): ( meters, kilograms, Kelvins, Newtons = kg m/s^2, Pascals = N/m^2, Density = kg/m^3, Speed = m/s, Equiv. Area = m^2 ) United States customary units (US): ( inches, slug, Rankines, lbf = slug ft/s^2, psf = lbf/ft^2, Density = slug/ft^3, Speed = ft/s, Equiv. Area = ft^2 )

TARGET_CL.description: Target coefficient of lift for fixed lift mode (0.80 by default)

TEMPERATURE_LIMITS.description: Temperature limits for incompressible flows (0.0, 5000.0 K by default).

THERMAL_CONDUCTIVITY_CONSTANT.description: Thermal conductivity used for heat equation

THERMAL_EXPANSION_COEFF.section: NONEQUILIBRIUM GAS, IDEAL GAS, POLYTROPIC, VAN DER WAALS AND PENG ROBINSON CONSTANTS, CoolProp library
THERMAL_EXPANSION_COEFF.description: Thermal expansion coefficient (0.00347 K^-1 (air)) Used with Boussinesq approx. (incompressible, BOUSSINESQ density model only)

THERMODYNAMIC_PRESSURE.section: NONEQUILIBRIUM GAS, IDEAL GAS, POLYTROPIC, VAN DER WAALS AND PENG ROBINSON CONSTANTS, CoolProp library
THERMODYNAMIC_PRESSURE.description: Thermodynamics(operating) Pressure (101325 Pa default value, only for incompressible flow and FLUID_MIXTURE)

THETA_INTERIOR_PENALTY_DG_FEM.description: Factor for the symmetrizing terms in the DG FEM discretization (1.0 by default)

THICKENED_FLAME_CORRECTION.description: Thickened flame correction Approximate the thickness of the flame and suppress source terms and enhance diffusivity in cells with a lengthscale higher than the flame thickness.

TIME_AVG_EXP_CONST.description: Fixed sample weight used when TIME_AVG_METHOD= EXPONENTIAL, in (0, 1]. Smaller values average over a longer effective time window (slower to respond, smoother); larger values respond faster but average over fewer effective samples. Unused (and unchecked) when TIME_AVG_METHOD= CUMULATIVE.

TIME_AVG_METHOD.description: Running-average method for all TIME_AVERAGE/BACKSCATTER volume output fields (CUMULATIVE, EXPONENTIAL). CUMULATIVE (default) is the classic running average: every sample is weighted equally (1/N). EXPONENTIAL blends every new sample in with a fixed weight (TIME_AVG_EXP_CONST) instead, so older samples are progressively down-weighted rather than counting equally forever.

TIME_DISCRE_SPECIES.description: Time discretization for species equations (EULER_IMPLICIT, EULER_EXPLICIT)

TIME_DOFS_ADER_DG.description: Number of time DOFs for the predictor step of ADER-DG (2 by default)

TIME_INSTANCES.description: Integer number of periodic time instances for Harmonic Balance

TIME_MARCHING.description: Unsteady simulation (NO, TIME_STEPPING, DUAL_TIME_STEPPING-1ST_ORDER, DUAL_TIME_STEPPING-2ND_ORDER, HARMONIC_BALANCE)

TIME_STEP.description: Time Step for dual time stepping simulations (s) -- Only used when UNST_CFL_NUMBER = 0.0 For the DG-FEM solver it is used as a synchronization time when UNST_CFL_NUMBER != 0.0

TOPOLOGY_OPTIMIZATION.description: "Classic" density approach to topology optimization. Each element is assigned a density variable that is used to penalize its stiffness.

TOPOL_OPTIM_FILTER_KERNEL.description: Filtering is required to avoid numerical issues, see [Sigmund, 2007] (DOI 10.1007/s00158-006-0087-x). Currently available options: CONSTANT; CONICAL (default); GAUSSIAN; DILATE; ERODE. The filter can have multiple sequential stages (2 in this case).

TOPOL_OPTIM_FILTER_RADIUS.description: Each kernel can have its own radius (R1, R2, ...) or one value can be specified for all.

TOPOL_OPTIM_KERNEL_PARAM.description: The Gaussian, Erode, and Dilate filters, have a constant parameter. Again this can be a list.

TOPOL_OPTIM_OUTFILE.description: Output file for the derivatives of the OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION w.r.t. the design densities.

TOPOL_OPTIM_PROJECTION_PARAM.description: The continuous Heaviside function (step) approximations require a parameter, large value equals more discrete.

TOPOL_OPTIM_PROJECTION_TYPE.description: After the filtering, a projection step can be applied to increase the solid-void contrast, i.e. the discreteness of the solution. Options: NO_PROJECTION (default); HEAVISIDE_UP; HEAVISIDE_DOWN.

TOPOL_OPTIM_SEARCH_LIMIT.description: The filtering may become very expensive if the mesh has very refined regions. If different from 0 this option mitigates that by limiting the "logical radius" (for immediate neighbors that radius is 1, etc.).

TOPOL_OPTIM_SIMP_EXPONENT.description: The penalization exponent for the Simplified Isotropic Material with Penalization.

TOPOL_OPTIM_SIMP_MINSTIFF.description: The stiffness of void elements (normalized by ELASTICITY_MODULUS)

TOTAL_DV_PENALTY.description: Penalty weight value to maintain the total sum of DV constant

TRANSIENT_TERM_REMOVAL_FACTOR.description: Heuristic parameter influencing the effect of the pseudo time derivative in the momentum coefficients for the pressure correction equation (float [0,1], default=0.0)

TRANSLATION_RATE.description: Translational velocity (m/s or ft/s) in the x, y, & z directions

TURBOMACHINERY_KIND.description: Specify kind of architecture for each zone (AXIAL, CENTRIPETAL, CENTRIFUGAL, CENTRIPETAL_AXIAL, AXIAL_CENTRIFUGAL)

TURBO_PERF_KIND.description: types of turbomachynery Performance Calculations. OPTIONS: see TurboPerfKind_Map Default: TURBINE

TURBULENT_CONDUCTIVITY_MODEL.description: Definition of the turbulent thermal conductivity model for RANS (CONSTANT_PRANDTL_TURB by default, NONE).

TURBULENT_MIXINGPLANE.description: Specify option for turbulent mixing-plane (YES, NO) default NO

TURB_FIXED_VALUES.description: Fix turbulence quantities to far-field values inside an upstream half-space

TURB_FIXED_VALUES_DOMAIN.description: Shift of the half-space on which fixed values are applied. It consists of those coordinates whose dot product with the normalized far-field velocity is less than this parameter.

UNST_ADJOINT_ITER.description: Starting direct solver iteration for the unsteady adjoint

UNST_CFL_NUMBER.description: Unsteady Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy number of the finest grid

UPDATE_AOA_ITER_LIMIT.description: Maximum number of iterations between AoA updates

UPDATE_BCTHRUST.description: Number of times BC Thrust is updated in a fix Net Thrust problem (5 by default)

UPDATE_IH.description: Number of times Alpha is updated in a fix CL problem.

USER_SCALAR_NAMES.description: Names of the user defined (auxiliary) transport equations.

USER_SOURCE_NAMES.description: Names of the source terms for the user defined transport equations. The source term has the form S = S_production + S_consumption * Y, with Y the mass fraction of the user scalar S = S_production + S_consumption * X, with X the mole fraction of the user scalar The second term can have the name "zero" or "null" to indicate that only a total source will be used.

USE_ACCURATE_FLUX_JACOBIANS.description: Use numerically computed Jacobians for AUSM+up(2) and SLAU(2) Slower per iteration but potentialy more stable and capable of higher CFL

USE_ACCURATE_TURB_JACOBIANS.description: Use numerically computed exact Jacobians for turbulence models Slower per iteration but potentialy more stable and capable of higher CFL

USE_AUTOMATIC_RELAXATION_FACTORS.description: Decide if automatic relaxation factors for pressure and momentum should be used or not. If set to NO, the value from RELAXATION_FACTOR_PRESSURE is used. default NO

USE_EXACT_HLLC_JACOBIANS.description: Use exact HLLC Jacobians with wave speeds held fixed (NO, YES). The default retains the previous approximation; wave-speed derivatives are omitted in both modes.

USE_LUMPED_MASSMATRIX_DGFEM.description: Use the lumped mass matrix for steady DGFEM computations (NO, YES)

USE_PINN.section: NONEQUILIBRIUM GAS, IDEAL GAS, POLYTROPIC, VAN DER WAALS AND PENG ROBINSON CONSTANTS, CoolProp library
USE_PINN.description: Use physics-informed neural network for calculation of the fluid caloric properties.

USE_VECTORIZATION.description: Use the vectorized version of the selected numerical method (available for JST family and Roe). SU2 should be compiled for an AVX or AVX512 architecture for best performance. NOTE: Currently vectorization always used for schemes that support it.

VALUE_OBJFUNC_FILENAME.description: Output Objective function (in tecplot .dat or .csv format)

VENKAT_LIMITER_COEFF.section: SLOPE LIMITER AND DISSIPATION SENSOR DEFINITION
VENKAT_LIMITER_COEFF.description: Coefficient for Venkatakrishnan-type limiters (upwind scheme). A larger value decreases the extent of limiting, values approaching zero cause lower-order approximation to the solution (0.05 by default)

VISCOSITY_MODEL.description: Viscosity model (SUTHERLAND, CONSTANT_VISCOSITY, POLYNOMIAL_VISCOSITY, FLAMELET, CANTERA).

VISUALIZE_CV.description: Node number for the CV to be visualized (tecplot) (delete?)

VOLUME_OUTPUT.description: Volume output fields/groups (use 'SU2_CFD -d <config_file>' to view list of available fields)

VOLUME_OUTPUT_PRECISION.description: Floating-point type of the fields of the volume and surface files (CGNS and Paraview XML): SINGLE or DOUBLE. The CGNS coordinates are always in double precision, the Paraview XML coordinates follow this option. SINGLE (about 7 digits) is enough to view the results; use DOUBLE when the values are processed further, e.g. to compare two solutions or to match the points of periodic surfaces.

VT_RESIDUAL_LIMITING.section: NONEQUILIBRIUM GAS, IDEAL GAS, POLYTROPIC, VAN DER WAALS AND PENG ROBINSON CONSTANTS, CoolProp library
VT_RESIDUAL_LIMITING.description: Specify if there is VT transfer residual limiting

WALLMODEL_B.description: The wall function model constant B

WALLMODEL_KAPPA.description: The von Karman constant, the constant below only affects the standard wall function model

WALLMODEL_MAXITER.description: [Expert] Max Newton iterations used for the standard wall function

WALLMODEL_MINYPLUS.description: The y+ value below which the wall function is switched off and we resolve the wall

WALLMODEL_RELFAC.description: [Expert] relaxation factor for the Newton iterations of the standard wall function

WALL_ROUGHNESS.description: The equivalent sand grain roughness height (k_s) on each of the wall. This must be in m. This is a list of (string, double) each element corresponding to a wall marker.

WEAKLY_COUPLED_HEAT_EQUATION.description: Enable heat equation for incompressible flows

WINDOW_FUNCTION.description: Window used for reverse sweep and direct run. Options (SQUARE, HANN, HANN_SQUARE, BUMP) Square is default.

WINDOW_START_ITER.description: Windowed output time averaging Time iteration to start the windowed time average in a direct run

WRT_FORCES_BREAKDOWN.description: Determines if the forces breakdown is written out

WRT_PERFORMANCE.description: Output the performance summary to the console at the end of SU2_CFD

WRT_RESTART_AVERAGES.description: Persist selected volume output fields (running averages) to a companion file, and restore them on restart so the running averages continue instead of resetting (NO, YES)

WRT_RESTART_COMPACT.section: DIRECT, ADJOINT, AND LINEARIZED PROBLEM DEFINITION
WRT_RESTART_COMPACT.description: Only save the minimum required variables for restarting to restart files (NO, YES). If this option is set to NO, then all fields will be written to all output files. To minimize the size of other output files (e.g. paraview, tecplot) by not including default restart fields in them, add the keyword COMPACT to VOLUME_OUTPUT.

WRT_RESTART_OVERWRITE.description: Overwrite or append iteration number to the restart files when saving

WRT_SURFACE_OVERWRITE.description: Overwrite or append iteration number to the surface files when saving

WRT_VOLUME_OVERWRITE.description: Overwrite or append iteration number to the volume files when saving

WRT_ZONE_CONV.description: Determines if the convergence history of each individual zone is written to screen

WRT_ZONE_HIST.description: Determines if the convergence history of each individual zone is written to file
